title: Passed without a committee hearing, year by year
question: How much of what the Board of Supervisors adopts skips committee, and is that share growing?
finding: Of 8,069 resolutions, motions and ordinances the Board adopted from 2019 to 2026, 1,734 (21%) were “referred for adoption without committee reference” and adopted with no committee hearing, typically 7 days after introduction. The share has stayed between 18% (2019) and 25% (2021) with no steady rise. Only 17 of the 1,734 name $100,000 or more in their title. 95% of all resolutions and motions were settled at the first Board meeting that took them up. On the land-use files whose vote counts are on disk, 95% of 773 final roll calls had no vote against. Among contract, grant and lease files alone, the site’s “The same winners, year after year” page counts 29 with no committee hearing and 107 sent to the full Board as a committee report.
how: From the action history of every Board file introduced since December 2018 and passed: a file counts when its history carries the Board’s own wording “referred for adoption without committee reference”. The year is the year of the Board’s final vote. “No hearing on record, not so referred” counts resolutions and motions with no dated committee action and no such referral. “Settled at one Board meeting” means the full Board acted on the file on a single date (ordinances, which need two readings, are left out). Days run from introduction to the final vote. The roll-call column uses the Board’s land-use files only (appeals, zoning, landmarks, liquor licences), the one set for which each vote was collected.
limits: Adoption without committee reference is the Board’s own recorded procedure, printed in each file’s public history. The published history does not mark the consent calendar and holds no vote counts outside land-use files, so “unanimous” cannot be counted for all files. An item adopted quickly was still voted on in public by the full Board. A unanimous vote often follows changes negotiated in committee. What would settle a row: the minutes of the meeting. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
